subject.title: EPERM crashes on database files during active locks in applyPrivateModeSync

question: Should OpenClaw tolerate EPERM from chmod on active SQLite WAL/SHM sidecars when the target is not already private and the filesystem probe succeeds?
rationale: The current behavior is deliberate security hardening from the prior fix, so changing it requires maintainer intent on the availability-versus-permission-enforcement boundary.

options.title: Require targeted repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open but ask for logs or a focused test showing active SQLite sidecar locks hitting the current rethrow branch before weakening the policy.

options.title: Allow a narrow sidecar exception
options.body: Accept a scoped fix limited to SQLite sidecars, with tests that preserve fail-closed behavior for ordinary ownership or broad-permission EPERM.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed policy
options.body: Treat broad-permission EPERM as a security signal and close only if maintainers decide availability should not override this hardening case.

recommendation.title: Require targeted repro first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open but ask for logs or a focused test showing active SQLite sidecar locks hitting the current rethrow branch before weakening the policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored the current narrowed EPERM policy and is the clearest owner for the security-boundary decision.
